note: General care guidance for common plants of Indore / central India. Ids match the species labels of the plant-identification model.

plants.name: Banyan

care.water: Low once established; water young trees weekly

plants.uses: National tree of India; shade tree with aerial prop roots; sacred and medicinal (latex, bark).
problems: Scale insects and mealybugs on young shoots
Sooty mould where sap-sucking insects are present

plants.name: Peepal (Sacred fig)

care.soil: Any soil, tolerates poor and rocky ground

plants.uses: Sacred tree with heart-shaped leaves and a long drip tip; shade and medicinal uses.
problems: Psyllids and scale insects causing leaf curling

plants.name: Neem

care.water: Drought tolerant; water young plants weekly

plants.uses: Medicinal tree; neem oil and leaf extract are widely used as natural pesticides.
problems: Neem dieback (Phomopsis fungus) with drying twigs
Tea mosquito bug damage on shoots

plants.name: Mango

care.water: Regular watering for young trees; stop before flowering

plants.uses: India's national fruit; leaves used in festivals.
problems: Powdery mildew on flowers and young leaves
Mango hoppers and mealybugs with sooty mould

plants.name: Ashoka (Mast tree)
plants.uses: Tall, narrow avenue tree with wavy drooping leaves; common along Indore roads.
problems: Leaf spot and leaf blight in the monsoon

plants.name: Gulmohar
plants.uses: Ornamental shade tree with brilliant red-orange summer flowers and fern-like leaves.

plants.name: Amaltas (Golden shower)
plants.uses: Ornamental tree with hanging yellow flower chains; pods used in Ayurveda.

plants.name: Jamun

care.water: Moderate; regular in the first years

plants.uses: Purple summer fruit; seeds used traditionally for diabetes.

plants.name: Guava
plants.uses: Popular fruit tree; leaves used for herbal tea.

plants.name: Papaya
plants.uses: Fast-growing fruit plant; fruit and leaf extract are widely used.
problems: Papaya ring-spot and leaf-curl viruses (mosaic, curled leaves)

plants.name: Banana

care.soil: Rich, deep soil with organic matter

plants.uses: Fruit; leaves used as plates in festivals.
problems: Wind tearing of leaves (not a disease)

plants.name: Coconut palm
plants.uses: Fruit, oil and fibre; ornamental in gardens.

plants.name: Tamarind
plants.uses: Sour pods used in cooking; long-lived shade tree.

plants.name: Arjun
plants.uses: Medicinal tree; bark used in Ayurveda for heart health.

plants.name: Eucalyptus
plants.uses: Fast-growing tree for timber and eucalyptus oil.
problems: Leaf blight and leaf spots in humid weather
Gall wasps forming bumps on leaves

plants.name: Teak
plants.uses: Valuable timber tree, common in Madhya Pradesh forests; very large rough leaves.

plants.name: Drumstick (Moringa)
plants.uses: Pods and leaves are nutritious vegetables.

plants.name: Lemon / Citrus

care.water: Regular, let topsoil dry between waterings

plants.uses: Lemon, lime and orange; fruit and leaves are aromatic.
problems: Citrus leaf miner (silvery tunnels in leaves)

plants.name: Pomegranate
plants.uses: Fruit shrub; widely grown in Maharashtra and MP.

plants.name: Bamboo
plants.uses: Construction, crafts and ornamental hedges.

plants.name: Custard apple (Sitaphal)
plants.uses: Sweet winter fruit, common in central India.

plants.name: Bael
plants.uses: Sacred trifoliate leaves offered to Lord Shiva; fruit used for sherbet and medicine.

plants.name: Saptaparni (Devil's tree)
plants.uses: Avenue tree with leaves in whorls of 5–7; strongly scented flowers in October–November.
problems: Psyllids causing leaf galls and curling

plants.name: Ber (Indian jujube)
plants.uses: Thorny fruit tree; fruit eaten fresh in winter.
problems: Powdery mildew on leaves and fruit

plants.name: Rose

care.water: Regular, at the base, not on leaves

plants.uses: Most popular garden flower; petals for gulkand and rose water.

plants.name: Hibiscus (Gudhal)
plants.uses: Large red flowers used in worship and hair oil.
problems: Mealybugs (white cottony clusters) and sooty mould

plants.name: Bougainvillea

care.water: Low; flowers best when slightly dry

plants.uses: Hardy climber with colourful papery bracts.

plants.name: Marigold (Genda)
plants.uses: Festival flower; repels some soil pests.

plants.name: Jasmine (Mogra)
plants.uses: Fragrant white flowers for garlands.

plants.name: Night jasmine (Parijat / Harsingar)
plants.uses: Night-blooming white flowers with orange tubes; leaves used in Ayurveda.

plants.name: Oleander (Kaner)
plants.toxic: All parts are highly poisonous – keep away from children and animals
plants.uses: Hardy flowering hedge, common on road dividers.
problems: Oleander aphids (bright yellow) with sooty mould

plants.name: Yellow oleander (Peeli kaner)
plants.toxic: All parts, especially seeds, are highly poisonous
plants.uses: Ornamental shrub with yellow trumpet flowers.

plants.name: Crape jasmine (Chandni)
plants.uses: Glossy evergreen shrub with white pinwheel flowers.
problems: Mealybugs and whiteflies with sooty mould

plants.name: Ixora (Rugmini)
plants.uses: Hedge plant with round clusters of red or orange flowers.
problems: Aphids and scale with sooty mould

plants.name: Periwinkle (Sadabahar)
plants.uses: Hardy flowering plant; source of anti-cancer alkaloids.
problems: Root and stem rot in wet soil

plants.name: Lantana
plants.toxic: Leaves and unripe berries are toxic to animals
plants.uses: Colourful hedge plant; an invasive weed in forests.

plants.name: Calotropis (Aak / Madar)
plants.toxic: Milky latex is poisonous and harms the eyes
plants.uses: Wasteland shrub with waxy grey-green leaves; flowers offered to Lord Shiva.

plants.name: Adenium (Desert rose)
plants.uses: Ornamental succulent with a swollen stem and pink flowers.
problems: Root and stem rot from over-watering

plants.name: Tulsi (Holy basil)
plants.uses: Sacred medicinal herb grown in most Indian homes.

plants.name: Curry leaf
plants.uses: Aromatic leaves used in tempering.
problems: Psyllids and whiteflies with sooty mould

plants.name: Mint (Pudina)
plants.uses: Culinary and medicinal herb.

plants.name: Aloe vera

care.water: Low; water only when soil is dry

plants.uses: Medicinal gel for skin and burns.

plants.name: Henna (Mehndi)
plants.uses: Leaves give the natural mehndi dye; used as hedges.

plants.name: Money plant (Pothos)
plants.toxic: Mildly toxic to pets if chewed

care.water: When top 2–3 cm of soil is dry
care.soil: Any potting mix; grows in water too

plants.uses: Most common indoor climber; believed to bring prosperity.
problems: Yellow leaves from over-watering or root rot
Brown leaf spots (bacterial/fungal) in damp air
Brown tips from dry air or too much sun

plants.name: Snake plant
plants.uses: Hardy indoor plant with upright banded leaves.
problems: Root rot and mushy leaves from over-watering

plants.name: Areca palm
plants.uses: Feathery indoor palm.
problems: Brown leaf tips from dry air or salt build-up

plants.name: Croton
plants.toxic: Sap irritates skin; toxic if eaten
plants.uses: Grown for brightly coloured red-yellow-green leaves (the colours are natural, not disease).
problems: Leaf drop when moved or over-watered

plants.name: Spider plant
plants.uses: Easy hanging-basket plant with striped leaves and baby plantlets.
problems: Brown tips from fluoride or dry air

plants.name: Jade plant
plants.uses: Succulent with thick round leaves, kept for good luck.
problems: Root rot and soft leaves from over-watering
Leaf drop from cold or overwatering

plants.name: Rubber plant
plants.uses: Indoor plant with large glossy leaves.
problems: Leaf drop and yellowing from over-watering

plants.name: Coleus
plants.uses: Grown for its multicoloured leaves (the colours are natural, not disease).

plants.name: Brinjal (Eggplant)
plants.uses: Common vegetable crop.

plants.name: Okra (Bhindi)
plants.uses: Common summer and monsoon vegetable.
problems: Yellow vein mosaic virus (spread by whiteflies)

plants.name: Wheat
plants.uses: Main rabi cereal of Madhya Pradesh.

plants.name: Parthenium (Congress grass)
plants.toxic: Causes skin allergy and asthma – do not touch with bare hands
plants.uses: Invasive weed: uproot before flowering while wearing gloves; do not compost the flowering plants.

plants.name: Apple
plants.uses: Temperate fruit tree.

plants.name: Blueberry
plants.uses: Berry shrub.

plants.name: Cherry
plants.uses: Temperate fruit tree.

plants.name: Maize (Corn)
plants.uses: Kharif cereal crop.

plants.name: Grape
plants.uses: Fruit vine.

plants.name: Peach
plants.uses: Temperate fruit tree.

plants.name: Capsicum / Chilli
plants.uses: Vegetable and spice crop.

plants.name: Potato
plants.uses: Major rabi vegetable.

plants.name: Raspberry
plants.uses: Berry shrub.

plants.name: Soybean
plants.uses: Main kharif crop of Madhya Pradesh.

plants.name: Squash / Pumpkin
plants.uses: Vegetable creeper.

plants.name: Strawberry
plants.uses: Winter fruit crop.

plants.name: Tomato
plants.uses: Major vegetable crop.
